To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neuronal PC12 cells exposed to heat shock exhibited: (i) a 45% decrease in protein synthesis, (ii) an increased phosphorylation state of the protein synthesis elongation initiation factor eIF2 alpha, (iii) an increased phosphorylated state of the protein kinase C substrate, (iv) a decrease in phosphorylation of the amyloid precursor protein, (v) the appearance of two additional APP-like peptides, and (vi) the induction of heat-shock protein 72.
neuronal PC12 cells exposed to heat shock exhibit a reduction in total protein synthetic activity and an increase in the phosphorylation of APP.
(1) heat shock causes the appearance of two APP-like polypeptide bands not present in controls; (2) heat shock causes a reduction of APP phosphorylation, which is not due to hyperphosphorylated EF-2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neuronal protein synthesis in a model of heat shock.
the effects of heat shock on the expression and phosphorylation state of the amyloid precursor protein.
the study of the effects of stress on the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the phosphorylation of the Alzheimer amyloid precursor protein is decreased in response to heat stress in the neuronal PC12 cell line, but that the phosphorylation state and expression levels of elongation factor 1-alpha and elongation factor 3 are not altered.
heat-shocked PC12 cells exhibited a decrease in the phosphorylated state of APP.
neuronal PC12 cells exposed to heat shock undergo many of the changes associated with the heat-shock response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heat shock causes the induction of heat-shock proteins and a decrease in protein synthesis.

we have developed an in vitro model system for studying neuronal response to stress and that this model system will be useful for studying the effects of heat shock and other stressors on the synthesis and phosphorylation of APP.

heat-shocked neuronal PC 12 cells exhibit a number of features associated with the heat-shock response including a reduction in total protein production, the induction of a 72 kD heat shock protein, and an increase in eIF-2a phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heat shock can alter the phosphorylation state and expression of APP, a molecule implicated in the pathology of AD.
heat shock causes a significant decrease in APP phosphorylation and a significant increase in the number and abundance of APP isoforms.
heat shock can alter the expression and phosphorylation state of the APP protein in neuronal cells.
